dedupe_keys.name: ahn actueel hoogtebestand nederland national elevation model of the netherlands

description: AHN (Actueel Hoogtebestand Nederland) is the national high-resolution elevation dataset of the Netherlands, built from airborne laser scanning collected since 1997 by the water boards, provinces and Rijkswaterstaat. Successive national surveys are published, and the first part of AHN6 was released on 13 October 2025. Products include digital terrain models and digital surface models at 0.5 metre and 5 metre resolution as GeoTIFF and classified point clouds as LAZ, in the Dutch national grid with NAP heights (EPSG 7415), supplied in tiles of 6.25 by 5 kilometres. The data are open data available free without conditions, with AHN1 to AHN3 open since 2014. Caveats: each survey spans several years, so tiles differ in acquisition date, and surface models include vegetation and structures. It supports flood modelling, dike and levee inspection, drainage design and 3D city and utility modelling across Dutch infrastructure; a related record is the USGS 3D Elevation Program.
